topics.label: Lecture Introduction and Learning Objectives
topics.groupedBecause: The lecturer introduces herself, the course structure, and the core learning objectives concerning the causes and mechanisms of cancer.

topics.label: Foundations of Cancer Etiology: Genetics, Bad Luck, and Environmental Influences
topics.groupedBecause: These subtopics introduce cancer as an evolutionary and genetic disease, exploring how intrinsic cellular processes, stochastic bad luck, and environmental exposures interact based on epidemiological evidence.

topics.label: Pathogen-Driven Carcinogenesis and the Burkitt Lymphoma Model
topics.groupedBecause: These subtopics discuss how infectious pathogens contribute to malignancy, focusing on Burkitt lymphoma as a case study of viral and parasitic co-factors driving genetic translocations.

topics.label: Chemical and Physical Mutagens and Xenobiotic Activation
topics.groupedBecause: These subtopics examine how physical radiation and chemical exposures undergo direct action or metabolic activation via xenobiotic pathways to form mutagenic DNA adducts.

topics.label: Tumor Promotion, Chronic Inflammation, and Host Susceptibility
topics.groupedBecause: These subtopics address non-mutagenic mechanisms of carcinogenesis, illustrating how promoters, inflammatory microenvironments, and host developmental stages permit tumor outgrowth.

topics.label: Methods for Identifying and Testing Carcinogenicity
topics.groupedBecause: These subtopics explore the genomic, epidemiological, in vivo, and in vitro experimental strategies used to detect carcinogen exposures and evaluate carcinogenic potential.

topics.label: Lecture Summary and Risk-Benefit Considerations
topics.groupedBecause: The lecturer concludes the lecture by summarising the environmental basis of cancer and discussing the balance between practical benefits and carcinogenic risks in daily life.
